title: Student Privacy & Campus Surveillance for Beginners
metaDescription: Learn to protect your student privacy from campus surveillance, proctoring software, and school monitoring. Essential guide for students and parents.
intro: Students today face unprecedented digital surveillance on campus and during online learning. From proctoring software that monitors your every move to school-issued devices tracking your activity, understanding your privacy rights is crucial for academic success and personal security.
prerequisites: Access to school devices or accounts

steps.title: Understand Your FERPA Rights
steps.description: The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) protects your educational records and gives you control over who can access your academic information.
actions: Request a copy of your school's FERPA policy from the registrar's office
Learn what information is considered 'directory information' at your school
Understand how to opt out of directory information sharing
Know your rights to access and review your educational records
steps.proTip: FERPA rights transfer from parents to students when you turn 18 or enter college, so make sure you understand these protections.

steps.title: Audit Your School-Issued Devices
steps.description: School-provided laptops, tablets, and accounts often come with monitoring software that can track your activity, location, and even access your camera or microphone.
actions: Check for monitoring software like GoGuardian, Securly, or LanSchool on your device
Review what apps and programs are installed that you didn't authorize
Understand your school's acceptable use policy for devices
Create separate personal accounts for non-school activities
steps.warning: Never assume school devices are private - treat them as if administrators can see everything you do.

steps.title: Navigate Proctoring Software Safely
steps.description: Online proctoring tools like Respondus Monitor, Proctorio, and Honorlock can access your webcam, microphone, screen, and browser activity during exams.
actions: Read the privacy policy of any proctoring software before agreeing to use it
Secure your testing environment by removing personal items from view
Use a dedicated browser like a privacy-focused browser for exams to isolate the session
Understand what data is recorded and how long it's stored
steps.proTip: Most proctoring software requires extensive permissions - only grant these during actual exam periods and revoke them immediately after.

steps.title: Control Your EdTech Data
steps.description: Educational technology platforms collect vast amounts of data about your learning habits, performance, and behavior that may be shared with third parties.
actions: Review privacy settings in all educational apps and platforms you use
Limit data sharing to only what's necessary for coursework
Ask teachers and administrators about data retention policies
Opt out of marketing and research data collection when possible

steps.title: Protect Your Personal Digital Life
steps.description: Separate your academic digital presence from your personal online activities to maintain privacy and prevent academic consequences for personal choices.
actions: Use different browsers for school and personal activities
Create separate email accounts for academic and personal use
Avoid using school WiFi for personal browsing when possible
Review social media privacy settings to limit school access to personal posts
steps.proTip: Consider using a privacy-focused browser for personal browsing on school networks to prevent tracking and maintain separation between academic and personal activities.

steps.title: Know Campus Surveillance Systems
steps.description: Modern campuses use extensive surveillance including security cameras, WiFi monitoring, ID card tracking, and facial recognition systems.
actions: Request information about what surveillance systems your school uses
Understand where cameras are located and what they record
Learn about WiFi logging and network monitoring policies
Know your rights regarding surveillance footage and data requests
steps.warning: Campus surveillance data may be shared with law enforcement or used in disciplinary proceedings - be aware of what's being monitored.

steps.title: Advocate for Better Privacy Practices
steps.description: Students have power to influence school privacy policies through proper channels and collective action.
actions: Join or form student privacy advocacy groups on campus
Attend school board meetings or administrative hearings about privacy policies
Submit formal requests for privacy policy changes through student government
Document privacy violations and report them to appropriate authorities

pro_tips: Always read privacy policies before agreeing to use educational software - look for data sharing, retention periods, and third-party access clauses.
Use separate devices for personal activities when possible, or partition your digital life with different browsers and accounts for school vs. personal use.
Document any privacy violations by taking screenshots and keeping records - this evidence may be crucial if you need to file complaints or appeals.
Connect with other students facing similar privacy concerns - collective advocacy is often more effective than individual complaints.
Stay informed about your state's student privacy laws, which may provide additional protections beyond federal FERPA requirements.

faqs.question: Can my school monitor my personal social media accounts?
faqs.answer: Schools cannot directly access your private social media accounts, but they may monitor public posts or investigate reports of concerning content. Some schools require students to friend official accounts or may use social media monitoring services to track mentions of the school.

faqs.question: Is it legal for proctoring software to record me during exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, proctoring software can legally record you during exams if you consent to its use. However, you have the right to know what's being recorded, how long recordings are stored, and who has access to them. Some institutions offer alternative testing arrangements if you object to proctoring software.

faqs.question: Can I refuse to use school-issued devices that have monitoring software?
faqs.answer: This depends on your school's policies. K-12 students typically must use assigned devices, but may have rights to privacy on personal devices. College students often have more options, including using personal devices or accessing alternative computing resources.

faqs.question: What should I do if my school violates my privacy rights?
faqs.answer: Document the violation, review your school's complaint procedures, and consider contacting the Family Policy Compliance Office (FPCO) if FERPA rights are violated. You may also want to consult with student advocacy groups or legal aid services.

faqs.question: How can I tell if my school computer has monitoring software installed?
faqs.answer: Check your installed programs list for software like GoGuardian, Securly, LanSchool, or similar names. Look for unfamiliar browser extensions or programs that start automatically. You can also ask your IT department directly about monitoring software on school devices.
